title: Building a time-series inference platform. Looking for feedback from traders
author: network-kai
selftext:
I'll be honest, I'm currently working with a time-series inference platform right now, helping out with comms and outreach. I'm looking for people who do agentic trading to try to product out and give their feedback.

It's called [Ephermis](https://ephemeris.cascade.industries/), and it provides access to 7 of the leading time-series foundation models under one API key. So it's got Amazon's Chronos-2, Google's TimesFM-2.5 (not FM-3 purely because Google are strict about it being used for trading), IBM models, and Mistral's recent Timestral model.

I'm not personally a trader. I used to be, but if I'm being real I found it too stressful.

I know a lot of people here use LLMs in their trading stats. Do you ever plug them into a TSFM of your own? I also know a lot of you like to hook up Jev (or another decision model into the flow).

The founder of the company  [wrote a pretty neat piece](https://x.com/cascade_sn91/status/2117296098666787065) about how to use TSFMs combined with LLMs along with a decision model.

So if that's something you're into it's definitely possible.

TSFMs are pretty small, so self-hosting is definitely possible, but it can get kinda tiring if you're constantly switching between models. I've seen traders before use Ephemeris because it lets you swap them on the fly. It also lets you combine them ([which we've found gives you higher results than leading models alone](https://www.cascade.industries/weir/)). We call this the *Ensemble Model*.

The thing is, this is obviously a product-facing post, so I understand the skepticism this will naturally bring. The service offers 2000 credits for free so people can play around. It gives you a good amount to give it a go without paying anything.

I'm not the founder, but I work close with him. I'm happy to help demo stuff, address question and feedback, and even if you're really not a fan that's useful, too.

  
The website is a little barebones, so I'll drop the X account, which gives more context. [https://x.com/cascade\_sn91](https://x.com/cascade_sn91)

comments.author: investigatormaker
comments.body:
For Ephemeris, give traders one reproducible comparison: the same timestamped dataset and forecast horizon through a single TSFM and your Ensemble Model, with a held-out period. Report forecast error, latency, and credits consumed separately; “higher results” doesn’t tell someone which trade-off improved. That makes the free credits a way to answer a specific question rather than an open-ended demo.
